newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Gilt vol falls,short stg calm pre-election.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Gilt vol falls,short stg calm pre-election.

text.p: Implied volatility of June gilt options fell on Monday despite the impending British election on May 1, and short sterling volatility was steady along the curve, options participants said.
"We could have a small panic on Wednesday," said Mourad Amellel, managing director of Transoptions Finance in London.
"But the market is expecting that Labour will win, and everything is already priced in."
Implied volatility of June at-the-money gilt options dropped by around half a point to 7.5-8.0 percent from Friday's levels, said one broker from a UK firm.
Later months held steady, the broker added, with September at 7.32 percent bid, and December 1997 and March 1998 both at 7.42 percent bid.
At-the-money June short sterling options were quoted at an implied volatility of nine percent, said Amellel, September at 11.11 percent and December at 12.50 percent.

Polls consistently forecasting a comfortable majority for the opposition Labour party have stripped the market of pre-election uncertainty, options dealers said. The latest five opinion polls put Labour between 16 and 24 points ahead of the ruling Conservatives.
Trading was thin in the run-up to the election.

In gilt options, the most active strikes were July 109-00 puts and July 109-00 calls, which traded 350 lots apiece. June gilt futures were trading at 109-04 at 1107 GMT, 12/32 above Friday's closing price.
Short sterling put options traded 2,630 times at the June 93.25 strike.
June short sterling futures were quoted at 93.34 at 1107 GMT, unchanged from Friday's close and implying money market rates of 6.66 percent.
UK base rates currently stand at six percent, and are widely expected to rise soon after the election.
